output.summary: The user requires at least 40% of suspended accounts to be genuinely fraudulent to enable auto-suspension. The packet provides a 1.0% fraud base rate (100 fraudulent, 9,900 legitimate out of 10,000). With 96% sensitivity, 96 fraudulent accounts are caught. With 92% specificity (8% false positive rate), 792 legitimate accounts are incorrectly flagged (0.08 * 9,900). Total suspensions are 96 + 792 = 888. The precision (fraction of suspensions that are fraudulent) is 96 / 888 ≈ 10.8%. This is significantly below the 40% threshold.
key_claims: Calculated Precision: ~10.8% (96 true positives out of 888 total suspensions)
risks_or_flaws: The calculated precision of the auto-suspension policy is ~10.8%, which fails the explicit constraint requiring at least 40% of suspended accounts to be genuinely fraudulent. Enabling auto-suspension would result in suspending ~792 legitimate users for every 96 fraudulent ones.
output.verification_question: Does the security team accept a precision of ~10.8%, or is the 40% threshold a hard blocker for enabling auto-suspension?
